messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Microsatellite Data import
parts:
Hello,

The reason this is happening is because the "sep" argument is antagonistic to the "ncode" argument. If you have both sep and ncode, sep will win and obviously gives you incorrect results (the devel version of adegenet will give you a warning if this happens). The answer to the problem you are posting is to specify ncode = 3 and not sep = "". However, if I'm reading this correctly, you are having a problem where your data don't are not strictly 3-coded alleles.

If you have data where you have either 4 or 6 characters to encode alleles, the answer is to add zeros to the beginning of the 2code alleles with the `str_replace_all()` function from the stringr package. The example below shows how you can find an entry that has exactly two digits encoding the data (in the code [0-9]{2} means 2 of any digit, ^ means the beginning of the string element, and $ means the end).

library("stringr")
x <- data.frame(pop = c("A", "B"),
                x = c("1234", "567890"),
                y = c("098765", "4321"),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE
               )
x
#>   pop      x      y
#> 1   A   1234 098765
#> 2   B 567890   4321
to_find <- "^([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})$"
x[] <- lapply(x, FUN = str_replace_all, to_find, "0\\10\\2")
x
#>   pop      x      y
#> 1   A 012034 098765
#> 2   B 567890 043021

Hope that helps.

Best,
Zhian

On Mon, Oct 28, 2019 at 3:31 PM Silvia <silvia...@unitus.it> wrote:
Hi Guys,

I am facing some problems regarding the input file to be trasnformed into a genind object.
Since I am working with diploid microsatellites, I used the microbov dataset as example which was converted into a dataframe and the pop column removed:

data("microbov")
microbov
microbov_df <- genind2df(microbov)
microbov_df$pop <- NULL

Then, I transformed it again into a genind:

micro3_ind <- df2genind(microbov_df, sep = "", ploidy = 2, NA.char = "NA")
micro3_ind

Here is the problem. I don't get the same number of alleles, meaning that I'm using the wrong code.
> microbov
/// GENIND OBJECT /////////

 // 704 individuals; 30 loci; 373 alleles; size: 1.1 Mb

> micro3_ind
/// GENIND OBJECT /////////

 // 704 individuals; 30 loci; 213 alleles; size: 678.5 Kb


I think I can't use the ncode because at some point there are 2code alleles..
What am I doing wrong?
